The longest river in the world is the Nile.

To understand herd immunity, think of it like a firewall in computer security. If enough computers (or people) in a network are protected against a virus (or infectious disease), it becomes very difficult for an infected computer (or sick person) to spread the virus to other computers (or people) that aren't protected. Just as a strong firewall stops malware from jumping between devices, a high level of immunity in a population stops a disease from spreading easily.
